title: sigil-speech-bench-spec/1
description: Input of `Sigil.exe --headless speech-bench <spec.json> [--out <dir>]` (P7-A implements it in src-tauri/src/services/bench/speech.rs). Frozen by P7-S0: fields may be added (optional, with defaults that keep every earlier spec meaning the same), never renamed or removed. Unknown fields are errors (serde deny_unknown_fields), except `$comment` anywhere. Relative paths resolve against the spec file's folder. Secrets never appear in a spec: an API key is named by an environment variable (`options.apiKeyEnv`). Path fields (corpus.manifest, mt.set, tts.prompts, co_load.voice_changer_spec, hypotheses / rendered paths in options, and a bring-your-own engine model) expand `${NAME}` from the environment first, with two defaults when unset: SIGIL_P7_ROOT = %LOCALAPPDATA%/sigil-dev-cache/p7 and SIGIL_P7_CORPUS = ${SIGIL_P7_ROOT}/corpus; an unknown variable is an error.

name.description: Short id; names the default output folder (bench-results/speech/<name>-<timestamp>/).

seed.description: Seed of every pseudo-random choice the runner makes (item order shuffles for paced feeds, load jitter).

engines.description: Every engine the runs may use; ids are unique.

runs.description: Executed in order; run names are unique.

comment.description: Free-form notes, ignored by the runner.

lang.description: Lower-case BCP-47 base subtag as speech::lang::normalize writes it (en, ja, zh, ko, yue, es, de, fr, ru, pt); MT directions may carry a script / region (zh-Hant, pt-PT).

direction.description: MT direction <source>-<target> exactly as mt-bench writes it (en-ja, ja-en, en-zh-Hant).

corpus.description: The audio corpus (sigil-speech-corpus/1 manifest built by scripts/speech-bench/corpus/build_corpus.py) and the default item selection of the STT runs.

select.description: Which corpus items a run feeds. All filters combine (AND). Within a language, items keep the manifest's `rank` order, so `limit_per_language: k` takes the same k utterances under every condition (paired comparisons).

subset.description: A named subset of the manifest (`subsets`: core, snr_sweep, mic, real, quick, ...): its condition list.

kinds.description: synthetic = built from FLEURS + bleed; real = drop-in clips (corpus/real).

limit_per_language.description: Utterances per language (by rank), applied before conditions.

ids.description: Explicit item ids (overrides the other filters when non-empty).

id.description: Unique; names hypothesis / audio files and report rows.

backend.description: stt: the speech plugin's EngineKind wire names `whisper`, `http`, `sherpa-online`, `sherpa-offline`, `transcribe`, plus `pipeline` (the real speech pipeline: Silero VAD, router, two-pass; `options.route` is a RouteRequest), `crispasr` (R2T2 through the CrispASR runtime, prerequisite) and `hypotheses` (`options.path`: JSON lines {item, text} made elsewhere). mt: mt-bench's `nllb`, `openai`, `hypotheses`, plus `bergamot` (mt_local::bergamot) and `llama-server` (Sigil starts the bundled helper with catalog `model` and `variant`). tts: `local-tts` (in-process local_tts: Kokoro, Kitten, Piper, Pocket, Chatterbox-ort, sbv2), `tts-helper` (tts_helpers engine `options.helper`: qwen3, magpie, breeze, omnivoice, s2), `openai-speech` (any OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech server) and `rendered` (`options.dir` of <prompt id>.wav made elsewhere).

model.description: Model-store catalog id (stt/..., mt/..., tts/...; located with model_store::installed_path, never downloaded by the runner) or an absolute path for a bring-your-own model. Empty for backends without a model.

execution_provider.description: Requested device. Maps to the runtime variant (transcribe / llama-server / helpers: cpu -> best CPU variant, cuda -> cuda13, vulkan -> vulkan) or the ORT EP ladder (cuda, dml). The report records what was requested and what ran, with the reason of any fallback; a fallback is never hidden.

variant.description: Force a runtime pack variant (cpu, cpu-avx2, cpu-avx512, vulkan, cuda13); null = from execution_provider.

threads.description: Inference threads; null = the engine's default (speech::engine_api::EngineSpec.threads).

languages.description: stt: the corpus languages this engine is fed (default: every selected language); tts: the prompt languages it renders.

language_mode.description: stt: pass the item's language to the engine (given) or let it detect (auto).

directions.description: mt: directions this engine translates (default: every direction of the set).

options.description: Backend-specific settings, passed through. stt: speech::engine_api::EngineSpec.options (pipeline: `route` = a RouteRequest {language, tier, twoPass}; hypotheses: `path`; crispasr: `crispasrBackend`, and `modelFile` to pick a file of a catalog model that lists several). mt: mt-bench engine fields in camelCase (prompt, maxTokens, temperature, timeoutMs, baseUrl, beam, apiKeyEnv; hypotheses: path). tts: `voice` (every language) or `voices` {lang: voice}, `speed`, `helper` + `config` (tts-helper: the helper's camelCase start config), `baseUrl` / `apiKeyEnv` (openai-speech), `dir` (rendered). Never secrets: a key comes from the environment variable named by apiKeyEnv.

load_spec.description: Exactly bench::spec::LoadSpec (sigil-bench-spec/1 `load`): the GPU hammer and CPU burner threads at a duty cycle.

feed.description: How audio reaches an STT engine.

kind.description: utterance: the whole clip through AsrEngine::transcribe (model accuracy alone); stream: begin_stream / push_stream(chunk_ms) / end_stream (streaming engines: partials and the stream final); pipeline: the real speech pipeline from the clip (Silero VAD segmentation, router, two-pass finals; what users get), the item hypothesis is its finals joined (space, or nothing for ja / zh / yue).

pace.description: asap: as fast as the engine takes it (accuracy, compute); realtime: chunks at wall-clock pace (latency to final, first partial).

lead_silence_ms.description: Silence fed before the clip (pipeline: VAD pre-roll).

tail_silence_ms.description: Silence fed after the clip so a VAD can close the utterance.

gpu_lock.description: The dev rig's GPU timing lock (scripts/bench/gpu-lock.ps1). The runner never takes it: the campaign script acquires it (gpu-lock.ps1 -Run P7-A -Command ...), and the runner verifies that the lock file exists and its tag equals `tag` before a timing run, recording the owner in the report.

require.description: Refuse the run (status error) when the lock is not held by `tag`. Default: true for gpu_under_load and cpu_speed runs, false otherwise.

path.description: Lock file; null = $env:SIGIL_GPU_LOCK, else the gpu-lock.ps1 default.

thresholds.description: Gates applied to every engine aggregate of the run: metric name (an aggregate key of the report, e.g. rtf_p95, final_latency_ms_p95, vram_peak_mb, cpu_cores_mean, ttfa_ms_p95, latency_ms_p95) -> {min, max}. A metric the run did not produce fails as not measured.

prompts.description: JSON lines {id, lang, text, kind?, voice?, reference_voice?} (corpus/tts/prompts.jsonl from build_text_sets.py).

write_audio.description: <out>/audio/<engine>/<prompt id>.wav (PCM 16-bit at the engine's rate); always on for tts_listening.

intelligibility.description: Back-transcribe every rendering with an STT engine of this spec (its hypothesis lands in the item's `asr_text`; the scorer computes WER / CER against the prompt).

dnsmos.description: DNSMOS P.835 (bench/dnsmos-p835) per rendering: item fields dnsmos_sig / dnsmos_bak / dnsmos_ovrl.

speaker_similarity.description: CAM++ cosine (bench/campplus) between a cloning engine's rendering and the prompt's reference_voice clip: item field speaker_cosine.

set.description: An mt-bench corpus (JSON lines {id, source, target, src, ref | refs, ...}); corpus/mt/*.jsonl from build_text_sets.py.

context.description: previous: the engine's prompt gets the previous source line of the same document as context (LLM backends).

mode.description: accuracy (stt): hypotheses of every selected item, scored later by score/score_stt.py. cpu_speed (stt, mt, tts): compute, RTF, latency and process CPU with the engines on the CPU, optionally under the load simulator (a game on the same CPU). gpu_under_load (stt, mt, tts): the same with GPU engines under the GPU / CPU load simulator and the GPU timing lock, plus process VRAM. mt_quality (mt): hypotheses and latency over an MT set, scored by score/score_mt.py (chrF, MetricX). tts_listening (tts): renders every prompt to WAV with TTFA / RTF and optional automatic pre-screens, for tools/listening-test/make_tts_test.py.

engines.description: Engine ids; default: every engine whose task the mode takes.

warmup.description: Untimed items per engine first (not in the report's items).

repeat.description: Timed passes over the selection (speed modes); per-item timings are the median of the passes, hypotheses from the first.

load_profile.description: The bench contention profiles (bench::contention::PROFILES, without the stall): h1_vrchat_obs = conv hammer 70 % at 60 fps + 3 CPU threads at 50 %; h3_cpu_game = 4 CPU threads at 60 %; custom = `load` only. `load` overrides the profile's parts.

external_load.description: Free text recorded in the report when the load is real ("VRChat busy world + OBS NVENC 1080p60"): friends' live runs.

co_load.description: Optional: run the voice changer through the real harness (paced) in this process during the run, from a sigil-bench-spec/1 file of the user's voice (for example a filled-in copy of scripts/bench/specs/p3b/a/sve-gpu.template.json); its own paced numbers land in the run's co_load block.

timeout_s.description: Per item; an item over it is cancelled and reported as an error.

state_period_ms.description: Period of the GPU / host state series (bench::gpu_state::RunStateProbe); 0 = start and end only.

write_hypotheses.description: <out>/hyps/<run>.<engine>.jsonl (one line per item: the item object of the report).

export.description: <out>/export.json (sigil-speech-bench-export/1), always written: the friend-shareable subset (no audio, no paths, no host or user names).

include_text.description: Keep hypotheses / rendered text of synthetic items (never of real clips) in the export.
